name: maybe_Svc_Object_Shutdown
summary: Two-stage teardown of an object that owns a thread handle, a critical section and a service object: closes the handles under the CTR SVC locks, releases the sub-object at +0x18, resets the vtable to 0x007804BC and finishes with the critical-section base destructor.
evidence: The vtable literal at 0x001DC1B0 is 0x0075A4DC, whose slot +0x00 is this function and +0x04 is maybe_Svc_Object_Delete; the class-specific slots (+0x14 Ui_Object_DtorThunkC, +0x20 maybe_SvcObject_StartPendingState) are still unnamed, so the owner stays unproven and the maybe_ prefix stays. The body is not damaged - the svc 0x23/0x24 pairs are svcCloseHandle/svcWaitSynchronization1.

name: maybe_Sound_CloseObjectHandles
summary: Closes and clears the two kernel handles an object owns (+0x18 first, then +0x10) and returns the object; the handle-release step of a sound-subsystem teardown.
evidence: Disassembly is two copies of `bl 0x00118170; if ([p]) { svc 0x23; [p] = 0; }` applied to +0x18 and +0x10, then `return self`. The only named neighbour is Sound_Decoder_InitChannelTable (0x0054F18C), which is sound-subsystem code, so 'Sound' holds; 'Dsp' was unsupported and is dropped. No direct `bl` to this address exists in asm/text, so the caller edge is indirect and the object type stays open.

name: Shop_GetMaxAffordableCount
summary: Returns how many of an item the party can pay for: party gold (bag work+0x24A98 +0x28) divided by the item price (record +0x18), clamped to 9, or 0 for an unknown item.
evidence: Confirmed by the sibling Shop_CanAffordItem (0x00311134), which reads the same gold/price fields and shares the caller Ui_ItemScreen_HandleInput (0x001BFC50), and by the explicit `mov r0,#9` clamp in the disassembly; the divide helper 0x0011CFAC is a shift-subtract division loop, not a graphics call.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_DeactivateSubPanel
summary: Resets the sub-panel node at +0x1D0, inserts it into the window's list at +0x110 and broadcasts flag 0 (hide/close) to its children.
evidence: Disassembly: `bl 0x001EA614` re-links the list at +0x1D4, `bl 0x00123594(self, self+0x1D0)` inserts that node into the list at +0x110, then Ui_Object_BroadcastToChildren(self+0x1D0, 0). Both named callers (Ui_ItemScreen_HandleInput 0x001BFC50, Ui_ItemScreen_ConfirmEntryEx 0x001C0CF0) run it while closing the item page, so 'Detach' was the wrong verb - it re-inserts and hides. The list at +0x110 is not proven to be an inactive list, so the maybe_ prefix stays.

name: Field_Screen_Recreate
summary: Recreates the field screen object: releases the old 0x6C0-byte instance (Ui_Window_ReleaseResources + free), allocates a new 0x6C0 block from the field heap and constructs it with Ui_FieldScreen_Init.
evidence: Confirmed by three named callers in the scene flow (Field_InitSceneObjects 0x0019CD50, Ui_SceneFlow_ApplyFade 0x0019F878, Ui_SceneFlow_OpenScene5 0x001A1218) and by the explicit 0x6C0 allocation immediately followed by Ui_FieldScreen_Init; the old instance is released through Ui_Window_ReleaseResources and the slot is cleared.

name: maybe_FieldScene_Dtor
summary: Destructor of a large scene object: installs the caller's vtable, resets the actor slots, releases the sub-object at +0x10, destroys the lists at +0x10CC and +0x135E, re-links the list heads and re-seeds the 24-word template at 0x007291F0.
evidence: The vtable literal at 0x0021079C is 0x0075B574, but its class-specific slots (+0x14 func_00210A40, a destructor thunk, and +0x18 maybe_Ui_Panel_ApplyRectFromResource) do not name the class, and the ctor 0x0021066C is itself damaged. The scene reading still rests on the offsets and on Field_ResetActorSlots/Game_GetWork only, so the maybe_ prefix stays.
